title: Dragonwilds 1.0.1 Is a MUCH Bigger Update Than You Think…
author: ComfyQuesting
description:
RuneScape Dragonwilds 1.0.1 is HERE!! and this update is bigger than you might think! 🐉

Chapters
00:00 Intro
00:38 Characters saves
01:25 New special ranged attack
02:38 New ranged perks and ammunition
03:45 2 new slots and glory nerf
04:35 New jump attack
05:17 Inventory, storage and farming
06:19 Enemies combat and raid changes
07:18 Fixes and issues worth mentioning
08:19 Outro

New ranged special attacks, equipment changes, 40 inventory slots, new perks, and more!!

Here's everything you actually need to know about Dragonwilds 1.0.1. 💜

💬 What's your favourite change in this update?

#RuneScapeDragonwilds #Dragonwilds #RuneScape

transcript.text: So, Runescape Dragon Wars has just had its 1.0.1 update and there's actually quite a lot
here worth knowing. We've got new range special attacks, more inventory space, another equipment slot, and apparently
we can now launch ourselves onto enemies from above, which obviously sounds like something I'm going to try immediately
and probably get completely wrong. But, there's also some really important stuff here, especially if you've been having
problems with missing saves. So, rather than go through every tiny bug fix, I want to show you what's actually
changed, what it means for your character, and what I would be checking when I would next load up the game.
Because some of these changes are definitely going to affect how we've been playing since 1.0 launched. So,
let's get into it. So, missing saves and character recovery, and we need to talk about this because it's probably the
most important fix in this update. If you've been playing since 1.0 launched, you've probably seen people reporting
that their worlds have disappeared or their characters have become corrupted. And considering how many hours you can
put into this game, that's honestly just horrible. Jagex has already released fixes aimed at stopping more worlds from
disappearing, but 1.0.1 also targets worlds that were already missing. Now, there is something important here. This
doesn't mean every single lost save is guaranteed to come [music] back exactly how it was. Jagex has said they're still
investigating some remaining cases. So, if you've been affected, I would definitely check your worlds and
characters again after updating. And if your still isn't there, don't assume the problem has been completely resolved.
Keep an eye on the official updates and report what's happening. Hopefully, this means more people can actually get back
to playing. So, range weapons have new special attacks, and this is probably one of the most exciting ones because
range combat has a pretty big update. Instead of the different bows feeling quite so similar, short bows, long bows,
and crossbows now have their own special attacks. So, first the short bow gets rapid fire. This makes your character
jump backwards and fire three arrows in quick succession. And what's really nice is that you can actually change targets
between the shots. So, if you've got multiple enemies coming towards you, you've got a way to spread that damage
whilst creating a bit of distance. Then there's the long bow, which gets powershot. With this one, your character
takes a knee, draws the bow back, and fires a much more powerful shot over a long distance. So, this looks especially
nice when you want to attack something from further away. And finally, the crossbow gets heavy bolt. This one has a
short charge before firing a powerful bolt. But the important part is that it can also apply enchanted effects when it
hits. So, if you're using enchanted ammunition, that's definitely something worth trying out. Now, I'm not going to
tell you that one of these is automatically the best ranged weapon in the game because that depends on your
weapon, your ammunition, what you're fighting, and how you actually like playing. But I would definitely try the
new special on whichever ranged weapon you're currently using. You might find you prefer a completely different style
now. New ranged perks and better ammunition. So, alongside those new special attacks, we've also got some new
ranged perks. First is ammo recovery, and later you'll be able to unlock greater ammo recovery. These give you a
chance to recover arrows from enemies you've killed. So, it's not unlimited free ammunition, unfortunately, but if
you're constantly crafting arrows, this should help reduce how many you're getting through. Then we've got low
blow, and I actually quite like this one. If you hit an enemy in the legs or roughly the lower third of their body,
you can apply a slowing effect called hamstring. So, you can make certain enemies move more slowly for a short
time. There is a catch though. Tiny and colossal enemies are immune, so don't expect this to work on absolutely
everything. But against enemies it does affect, it could be really useful for keeping a
little distance. And there's another important ranged change. Rune arrows and bolts do more damage than adamant
ammunition. Jagex listed the damage multipliers as 4.9 versus 4.2. So, if you've been working towards rune
ammunition, it's now worth another look. Especially if your ranged progression was based on how much ammunition
performed before this update. Two accessory slots and the glory nerve. And this change affects equipment for pretty
much everybody. We've finally got a dedicated ring slot and an amulet slot, which means you can equip a ring and an
amulet at the same time. And honestly, I really like this because previously, you had to choose between accessories that
you might have wanted to use together. But there is also a nerf. The amulet of glory was apparently giving more bonus
than Jagex intended. So, those stats have now been reduced. And considering how much work can go into getting one,
that's probably not the news some people wanted. But it doesn't mean I'd immediately throw yours away. The patch
notes don't go with a complete before and after breakdown for every bonus. So, rather than calling it useless, I check
what it gives you now and compare it with the other accessories you've unlocked, especially because we've got
two slots to work with now. The best combination for your character might be different from what you're
using before. The new jump attack, and this is called death from above, which is a great name, by the way. Once you've
unlocked the perk in your skill tree, you can attack from above an enemy and come crashing down into them. But
there's something important you do need to know. You actually need enough height
to trigger it. Specifically, you need to be a little higher than the maximum height of a normal double jump from the
ground. So, if you're standing on flat ground, double jumping, and wondering why nothing is happening, that's probably
why. You can use an elevated position, and wind staff works with it as well. The damage also scales with your
equipped weapon, so what you're holding does matter. I can already see myself finding completely unnecessary ways to
jump onto enemies now. Apparently, just walking up and attacking something normally isn't exciting enough anymore.
Inventory storage and farming. [music] Now, onto some changes that make everyday playing a lot nicer. First, our
inventory has increased from 32 slots to 40. That's eight extra slots, which honestly is amazing because
I seem to leave my base to collect one thing in combat carrying just half of the map, so. And they've also improved
inventory sorting. You can sort by weight, which considers the combined weight of your stacks by type, by
latest, which puts your newest pickups first. And they fixed the chest sorting problem for controllers as well. We've
also got a new completed quest tab with short summaries of what has happened in the quest you finished. Which is quite
useful if you're anything like me and you can't remember the quest that you were doing three quests ago. And for
anybody that enjoys farming, they've added an ultra compost bin and a large compostable bucket. The larger bucket
can hold more, so that's a nice little quality of life improvement. There's also a change to the advanced spinning
wheel because you can now use overdrive on it. And that's not the most exciting change in the world, but if you're
spending hours gathering, farming, and organizing your base, little improvements like this really do add up.
Enemies, combat, and re-changes. Now, another change I think people are going to notice is how the enemies behave.
Jagex has reduced enemy aggro ranges across the game, so enemies shouldn't aggro issue from quite as far away. And
their respawn times have been increased, meaning they should stay dead for longer after you've cleared an area, which is
great if you're just trying to gather some resources without being interrupted every 10 seconds. [music] Inside the
Scourged Wilderness, they also fixed enemies and obstacles not responding correctly between runs. So, those should
now reset when you start another run. There are some other useful combat fixes as well. Enfeeble should now reduce
damage across enemy types as intended. They fixed a problem where some enemies not being infected by enchanted iron
bolts. And they've addressed a bug where using Titan's Wrath repeatedly could actually set your own character on fire,
which is just a bit unfair, isn't it? I'm trying to defeat the enemy, not cook myself. Now, the important fixes and new
issues that are worth mentioning. Players who picked up certain quest items too early through multiplayer
should no longer be blocked from progressing into the next region. There's also a fix for reputation
progression at Al Kharid's camp. The Regicide achievement has been fixed for cases where it didn't unlock after
defeating Kolodion. And Jagex has also addressed situations where Ascension crossbows weren't dropping from Kolodion
as intended. Which is definitely worth knowing if you've been farming that site. There are also fixes for teleport
related keyboard freezes, dedicated server building problems, and a few other issues that could interrupt your
progression. But because the update has only just released, I also want to mention something. Some players are
reporting that the fourth attack in the air magic staff combo isn't dealing damage properly after the patch, and
some people using older mods are reporting crashes, particularly with mods that change systems affected by this update.
Those are player reports, so I wouldn't assume absolutely everyone will experience them, but if something
suddenly isn't working after updating, it might be worth checking for known issues, especially if you are running a
modded game. Overall, I think this is a really nice update. It's not just bug fixes, there's actual gameplay changes
here that could make a difference to how you play. But I just want to know what you guys think. Which changes are you
the most happy about? If you've been having save problems, has this update actually fixed them for you? Let me know
in the comments, and if this helped you out, don't forget to leave a like, subscribe for more Dragon Wilds, and I
will see you guys in the next one. Bye.
